meta.headline: What a heat pump really costs to install, and what help is left in 2026
meta.seoTitle: Heat pump installation cost and incentives in 2026

dek.text: Against a furnace alone a heat pump costs more to install; against a new furnace and air conditioner together the studies disagree, and no federal tax credit applies to a heat pump installed in 2026.

assertions.text: Traditional fuel-fired heating systems averaged less than heat pump installations.
qualifications: question-1 says the heat pump also cools, in its unresolved callout on this claim.

assertions.text: Against a gas furnace plus AC, a heat pump's median installed cost is about the same, and there is no premium when comparing heating plus cooling like for like.
qualifications: The dek says the studies disagree rather than that they find parity; question-1 gives both sides.

assertions.text: No federal 25C credit applies to a heat pump placed in service after December 31, 2025, so none applies to 2026 installs.

description.text: A heat pump's installed price turns on what you compare it with and on electrical work, and no federal tax credit applies to one installed in 2026.

assertions.text: Installing a heat pump can require electrical panel and service upgrades that cost thousands of dollars.

sections.name: hook
sections.heading: Is the heat pump quote really the bigger cost?

sentences.text: Suppose the furnace gives out in midwinter and the installer offers a choice: a like-for-like furnace, or a heat pump at a noticeably higher price.

Whether that gap is real depends on what the heat pump is set against and on what the house needs to run it, and once the price is known, the next question is how much public money is still there to cut it.
So is the heat pump the dearer choice, or are the quotes pricing different jobs?

sections.name: question-1
sections.heading: What does a heat pump really cost to install, compared with the system you would buy anyway?

sentences.text: Some installers put the usual view bluntly; Atlas AC told viewers that "for upfront cost the furnace is going to be the cheapest the heat pump is going to be the most expensive".

assertions.text: Atlas AC said that for upfront cost the furnace is the cheapest option and the heat pump the priciest.

quote.text: for upfront cost the furnace is going to be the cheapest the heat pump is going to be the most expensive
quote.speaker: Atlas AC

sentences.text: EnergySage argues the reverse: "Installing a heat pump often costs less than simply swapping in a new AC and furnace or boiler".

assertions.text: EnergySage said installing a heat pump often costs less than swapping in a new AC and furnace or boiler.

quote.text: Installing a heat pump often costs less than simply swapping in a new AC and furnace or boiler
quote.speaker: EnergySage

sentences.text: Both can be right, because each sets the heat pump against a different purchase.

Set against heating alone, the heat pump costs more: in a national laboratory's database of 2,298 costed heating and cooling measures, fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations.

assertions.text: Among 2,298 costed HVAC measures in one database, traditional fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations.
qualifications: The unresolved callout after s08 says the heat pump also cools.

sentences.text: A separate model of US homes found that replacing the existing heater with a heat pump, rather than with the same kind of heater, cost an average of $6,600 more.

assertions.text: Replacing a house's existing heater with an 8.5 HSPF heat pump costs an average of $6,600 more than replacing it with the same technology.
qualifications: The unresolved callout after s08 says the heat pump also cools.

sentences.text: Neither comparison is like for like: each sets a heating-only purchase against a machine that also does the cooling, so the size of the premium depends on whether the household would have bought air conditioning anyway.

assertions.text: Among 2,298 costed HVAC measures in one database, traditional fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification: heating alone against heating plus cooling.

assertions.text: Heat pumps function as both air conditioners and heaters.

sentences.text: Count the air conditioner and the picture changes: in a single study's national medians, a heat pump cost $6,185 installed, $270 less than a natural gas furnace with central air, and more than 80 percent of the other systems' cost distributions overlapped with the heat pump's.

assertions.text: In one study's medians, a heat pump cost $6,185 to install, $270 less than a natural gas furnace plus AC, and more than 80% of the other systems' cost distributions overlap with the heat pump's.
qualifications: The unresolved callout after s13 says the furnace-plus-AC comparison is disputed.

blocks.caption: Median installed cost of heating and cooling systems of the same size, US, by system

rows.label: Natural gas furnace plus central air (same study)
Propane furnace plus central air (same study)
Electric baseboard heating plus central air (same study)

sentences.text: The same laboratory's model projects point the same way: for homes without cooling, an all-electric heating, cooling and hot-water upgrade cost $14,754 against $8,786 for gas, and the difference was almost exactly the $5,930 it costs to add cooling on its own.

assertions.text: In archetypal projects for homes without cooling, electric heating, cooling and hot-water upgrades cost $14,754 against $8,786 for gas equipment, a difference almost exactly the $5,930 cost of separately adding cooling, implying no premium when comparing like for like.
qualifications: The unresolved callout after s13 says the furnace-plus-AC comparison is disputed.

blocks.caption: Model project costs for homes without cooling: the all-electric upgrade, the gas upgrade and the cost of adding cooling on its own.

sentences.text: A Canadian model reaches a different verdict on the upfront price: heat pumps cost more upfront than gas heating with air conditioning there, yet they come out as the lowest-cost heating and cooling option for most households because they are efficient and double as the cooling.

assertions.text: The Canadian model finds heat pumps have higher upfront costs than gas-fired heating with air conditioning, and are the lowest-cost heating and cooling option for most households because of their efficiency and doubling as cooling.

sentences.text: An analysis from the NREL and LBNL national laboratories adds a condition: heat pumps meant to carry all of a home's heating are often more expensive to install than an air conditioner plus gas furnace, because bigger heating loads need bigger heat pumps, new wiring and sometimes panel or service upgrades.

assertions.text: Heat pumps designed to fully electrify space heating are often more expensive to install than an equivalent air conditioner plus gas furnace, mainly because larger heating loads require larger heat pumps, new wiring and sometimes electrical panel or service upgrades.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification itself: whole-home heating sizing makes the installed heat pump cost more than AC plus furnace.

sentences.text: Whether a heat pump matches a new furnace and air conditioner is not settled: the parity findings rest on a single study's national medians and on model projects, and the comparison reverses where the heat pump has to be sized to carry all of a home's heating.

assertions.text: Against a gas furnace plus AC, a heat pump's median installed cost is about the same, and there is no premium when comparing heating plus cooling like for like.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification; s12 gives the Canadian model that disagrees.

assertions.text: Heat pumps designed to fully electrify space heating are often more expensive to install than an air conditioner plus gas furnace, because of larger capacity, new wiring and sometimes panel or service upgrades.

sentences.text: If the only thing due is the air conditioner, the gap narrows: wholesale air-source heat pumps cost only $200 to $500 more than air conditioners of the same size.

assertions.text: Wholesale air-source heat pump prices are only $200 to $500 more than equivalently sized air conditioners.
qualifications: s14 says these are wholesale prices; s13 and s16 carry the installed cost.

sentences.text: A Minnesota cold-climate report quoting NREL's cost database put an efficient heat pump at $5,550 and an equally efficient central air conditioner at $5,180, a difference of $370.

assertions.text: In the NREL cost database quoted in the report, an efficient air source heat pump costs $5,550 and an equally efficient air conditioner $5,180, so the heat pump costs $370 more.
qualifications: The qualification callout after s17 gives the higher median premium in a later study and the whole-home sizing cost.

sentences.text: A later study's national medians from the same database, in the table above, tell a different story: there a heat pump cost about 32 percent more than a central air conditioner alone.

assertions.text: In the same study's medians, a central air conditioner costs $4,684 to install against $6,185 for a heat pump, so the heat pump costs about 32% more.

blocks.caption: A heat pump against an air conditioner of the same size: the wholesale premium and the database costs of efficient models.

sentences.text: Choosing a heat pump instead of a new air conditioner adds heating for little extra on wholesale prices and in one report's database costs, but a later study's medians put the premium higher, and a heat pump sized to heat the whole home can cost more than an air conditioner plus gas furnace.

assertions.text: Wholesale air-source heat pump prices are only $200 to $500 more than equivalently sized air conditioners.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification: wholesale and one database against a later study's medians and whole-home sizing.

assertions.text: Heat pumps designed to fully electrify space heating are often more expensive to install than an air conditioner plus gas furnace, because of larger capacity, new wiring and sometimes panel or service upgrades.

sentences.text: No study here is strong enough to decide whether a heat pump costs about the same as a central air conditioner of the same size: the cost-database report says their installed costs are very similar, while the national medians put the heat pump about 32 percent higher.

assertions.text: Heat pumps have installed costs very similar to traditional split system air conditioners with the same SEER value.
In the same study's medians, a central air conditioner costs $4,684 to install against $6,185 for a heat pump, so the heat pump costs about 32% more.

sentences.text: Within any comparison the price spreads widely: across 642 heat pump installations in the laboratory's database, the system's capacity and type, the home's floor area, the efficiency and the climate zone mattered most, and ground-source systems cost nearly three times as much as other types.

assertions.text: Across 642 heat pump installations, the most important cost variables were capacity, heat pump type, floor area, efficiency and climate zone, and ground source heat pumps cost nearly three times the total system cost of other types.
qualifications: The sentence names the database and its installations; s21 adds a second study's range.

sentences.text: Another study puts typical air-source installations at $5,000 to $10,000 in 2024 prices, varying with home size, efficiency, climate, labour and the installer's experience.

assertions.text: For air source heat pumps, typical installation costs range from $5,000 to $10,000 (2024 prices), and home size, efficiency, climate, labor and technician experience lead to different costs.

sentences.text: Then there is the electrical work: in a field test of cold-climate heat pump prototypes at 21 sites, 38 percent needed a new panel.

assertions.text: Across 21 sites installing cold-climate heat pump prototypes, 38% needed a new panel.
qualifications: The sentence names the population: 21 sites, cold-climate prototypes, a field test.

blocks.caption: Upgrades needed to install cold-climate heat pump prototypes in a field test, share of sites, and the cost of electrical upgrades

rows.label: Sites needing a new panel (21 field-test sites)
Sites needing new breakers for auxiliary heat (same sites)
Sites needing a service line upgrade (same sites)
Electrical upgrades, lowest total, labour and materials (same sites)
Electrical upgrades, highest total, labour and materials (same sites)

sentences.text: Where electrical upgrades were needed, labour and materials alone came to between $3,750 and $8,970, before the heat pump itself.

assertions.text: In that field test, the total costs for electrical upgrades varied between $3,750 and $8,970, for labor and materials only, not including the heat pump prototype.

sentences.text: Outside that small test, the laboratory's report gives $1,954 as the typical cost of a 200-amp panel upgrade, plus the wiring for each dedicated circuit to a new appliance.

assertions.text: The typical cost for a 200 amp electrical panel upgrade is $1,954, in addition to the electrical costs for each dedicated circuit run to new appliances.

sentences.text: The NREL and LBNL analysis puts panel, service-wire, transformer and pole upgrades at $2,000 to $30,000, though utilities may cover some of that, and notes that 50 to 60 percent of homes already have a panel above 150 amps.

assertions.text: Total costs to customers for upgrading electrical panels and potentially service wires, transformers and utility poles are estimated to range from $2,000 to $30,000, though utilities may cover some of these costs; 50% to 60% of homes already have a service panel greater than 150 amps.

sentences.text: How often a home needs this work is not well measured: the field test covered only 21 sites, and the national-laboratory analysis says further work is needed to learn how many homes need each kind of electrical upgrade and what it costs.

assertions.text: Across 21 sites installing cold-climate heat pump prototypes, 38% needed a new panel.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification: a small field test and an open question.

assertions.text: Further work is needed to understand how many homes would require these different types of electrical upgrades and their costs.

sentences.text: So the answer turns on the baseline: a heat pump costs more to install than a furnace alone, it can come out about even against a new furnace and air conditioner together unless it must be sized to carry all of the heating, and electrical work can add to the bill in either case.

assertions.text: Traditional fuel-fired heating systems averaged less than heat pump installations.
qualifications: s09 says the heat pump also cools.

assertions.text: Against a gas furnace plus AC, a heat pump's median installed cost is about the same, and there is no premium when comparing heating plus cooling like for like.
qualifications: s14 says this comparison is not settled.

assertions.text: Heat pumps designed to fully electrify space heating are often more expensive to install than an air conditioner plus gas furnace, because of larger capacity, new wiring and sometimes panel or service upgrades.
Installing a heat pump can require electrical panel and service upgrades that cost thousands of dollars.
qualifications: s26 says how often it is needed is not well measured.

sentences.text: That leaves the question of what public money is still there to bring the price down.

sections.name: question-2
sections.heading: What heat pump tax credits and rebates are actually left in 2026?

sentences.text: Older videos still promise federal help; The Thought Provocateur told viewers that "technically these heat pump tax credits based on the bill that was signed are available through 2033".

assertions.text: The Thought Provocateur said the heat pump tax credits in the signed bill are technically available through 2033.

quote.text: technically these heat pump tax credits based on the bill that was signed are available through 2033
quote.speaker: The Thought Provocateur

sentences.text: The credit did exist: from January 1, 2023, it was worth 30 percent of qualifying costs, up to $2,000 a year for a heat pump.

assertions.text: Beginning January 1, 2023, the home improvement credit equals 30% of qualified expenses, with a maximum of $2,000 per year for qualified heat pumps.

sentences.text: But its end was brought forward, and the IRS now says the credit will not be allowed for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025, so a heat pump installed in 2026 cannot claim it.

assertions.text: The IRS says the 25C energy efficient home improvement credit, whose termination was accelerated, will not be allowed for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
No federal 25C credit applies to a heat pump placed in service after December 31, 2025, so none applies to 2026 installs.

sentences.text: The Rebate Report pointed viewers to the other federal program instead: "the tax credit for heat pumps expired, but the rebate program for heat pumps survived".

assertions.text: The Rebate Report said the tax credit for heat pumps expired but the rebate program for heat pumps survived.

quote.text: the tax credit for heat pumps expired, but the rebate program for heat pumps survived
quote.speaker: The Rebate Report

sentences.text: Those federal rebates, however, are run by state energy offices and aimed at low- to moderate-income households.

assertions.text: The DOE home energy rebate programs are administered by State Energy Offices with the goal of serving low- to moderate-income households.
qualifications: The unresolved callout after s33 says how many households they could reach.

sentences.text: How many homeowners could use them is limited by design: the national-laboratory analysis estimated the $4.5 billion in electrification rebates could reach roughly up to 500,000 low-income households at $8,000 each, or 1 million moderate-income households at $4,000 each.

assertions.text: The $4.5 billion in point-of-sale electrification rebates could incentivize heat pumps for roughly up to 500,000 low-income households at $8,000 per household or 1 million moderate-income households at $4,000 per household.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification: an estimate of reach, not a count of claims.

sentences.text: The rollout has also been slow: in a state-by-state tracker, Alabama, Alaska and Arkansas had their applications only conditionally approved, with no expected launch date.

assertions.text: In the state tracker, Alabama, Alaska and Arkansas had HEAR and HER applications conditionally approved and no expected launch date for their rebate programs.
qualifications: The sentence names the tracker and the states; it does not give a national count.

sentences.text: Owen Marsh, in a video on what survived, counted "12 states and the District of Columbia" with programs launched as of June.

assertions.text: Owen Marsh said 12 states and the District of Columbia had launched as of June.

quote.text: 12 states and the District of Columbia
quote.speaker: Owen Marsh

sentences.text: How far the rollout has got is not settled here: the tracker is an earlier snapshot in which Alabama, Alaska and Arkansas were only conditionally approved, and it gives no national count of launched programs.

assertions.text: In the state tracker, Alabama, Alaska and Arkansas had HEAR and HER applications conditionally approved and no expected launch date for their rebate programs.
qualifications: This callout is the qualification: a tracker snapshot, not a national count.

sentences.text: Then, on May 29, 2026, the Department of Energy removed fuel-switching from the rebate: it now pays to upgrade existing electric equipment to more efficient electric equipment, and no longer to replace gas or other fossil-fuel appliances.

assertions.text: On May 29, 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy issued updated guidance under which HEAR rebates are no longer allowed for replacing gas or any other fossil fuel appliances.
DOE's program notice removes allowances for fuel-switching and allows HVAC rebates only for upgrading existing electric equipment to more efficient electric equipment.

sentences.text: According to North Carolina's state energy office, the change had to be in place by September 1, 2026.

assertions.text: North Carolina's state energy office says DOE's updated guidance must be implemented by Sept. 1, 2026.

sentences.text: State and utility programs remain, and some are generous: Massachusetts' Mass Save pays a whole-home rebate of $8,500, or $16,000 at the income-based level, against an average installation of $22,000 in its 2022 program data.

assertions.text: Mass Save's whole-home air source heat pump rebate is $8,500 standard or $16,000 income-based, against an average installation cost of $22,000 based on its program data for installations completed in 2022.
qualifications: s40 and the unresolved callout after s41 say this is a single program.

blocks.caption: Mass Save whole-home air-source heat pump rebate against the average installation cost

rows.label: Average installation cost (Mass Save program data, 2022 installations)

sentences.text: That is a single program: across the projects in the laboratory's database, which predates today's rules, the median total rebate was $1,327, about 21 percent of gross project cost.

assertions.text: The median total rebate per project was $1,327, or 21% of total gross project costs.
qualifications: The sentence says these are whole projects in that database, not heat pumps alone, and calls Mass Save one program.

blocks.caption: Rebates across the retrofit projects in the national laboratory database

Median total rebate per project (same database)
Mean total rebate per project (same database)

sentences.text: And a Canadian model found heat pumps there still cost more upfront, despite rebates meant to bring capital costs down.

assertions.text: Incentives do not always make a heat pump cheaper upfront: in the Canadian model, the higher upfront cost of heat pumps remains a barrier for households despite rebates intended to bring down capital costs.

sentences.text: No strong study decides whether state and utility rebates usually cover a large share of a heat pump's cost: the generous Mass Save figures are a single program's example, while the project database gives the typical share.

assertions.text: Mass Save's whole-home air source heat pump rebate is $8,500 standard or $16,000 income-based, against an average installation cost of $22,000 based on its program data for installations completed in 2022.
qualifications: s33 says this is one program and gives the typical share.

assertions.text: The median project rebate covered 21% of gross project cost, a minority share.
qualifications: s32 gives the generous exception; "usually" is the median from s33.

sentences.text: Nor can the evidence here say how often incentives make a heat pump cheaper upfront than a furnace and air conditioner: a national study's medians already put them close, while in the Canadian model heat pumps stayed dearer upfront despite rebates.

assertions.text: In one study's national medians a heat pump cost less to install than a natural gas furnace plus AC, and more than 80% of the cost distributions overlap.

Incentives do not always make a heat pump cheaper upfront: in the Canadian model, the higher upfront cost of heat pumps remains a barrier for households despite rebates intended to bring down capital costs.

sentences.text: For a heat pump installed in 2026, then, there is no federal tax credit, the federal rebate no longer pays to switch from gas, and state and utility rebates, where they exist, usually cut the price rather than erase it.

assertions.text: No federal 25C credit applies to a heat pump placed in service after December 31, 2025, so none applies to 2026 installs.
The federal HEEHR rebate no longer pays for fuel-switching, only for upgrading existing electric equipment.
The median project rebate covered 21% of gross project cost, a minority share.
qualifications: s32 gives the generous exception; "usually" is the median from s33.

sections.name: close
sections.heading: What to check before you sign

sentences.text: Start by naming the system you would install if the heat pump were off the table, whether that is a furnace on its own or a furnace with new central air, and judge every heat pump quote against that price.

Ask every installer up front whether your panel and service can carry the heat pump, and check your state energy office and your utility for rebates before you sign, setting aside any federal credit promised for a new install.
